title: Safely admit the exact production dependency audit to task verification
businessObjective: Restore deterministic machine verification of approved production-dependency audits without granting generic npm execution or changing application dependencies.
technicalObjective: Extend verify:task's safe required-command parser to accept only the literal npm audit --omit=dev command, preserve its true exit status, and add fail-closed parser coverage.
assumptions: npm audit --omit=dev is a registry-read-only dependency audit; it must not be replaced with install, update, fix, or force behavior.
The audit result is time-sensitive and a nonzero exit remains a real verification failure rather than a parser failure.
The finalized platform remains an immutable compatibility baseline and is never built, installed into, or modified by this task.
acceptanceCriteria: verify:task accepts exactly npm audit --omit=dev and executes it as npm with the fixed arguments audit and --omit=dev, without a shell.
verify:task rejects npm audit, npm audit fix, npm audit --omit=dev with any extra argument, npm commands with shell operators, and every other npm command as blocked.
The verifier preserves the audit process exit code: zero passes; nonzero or execution error fails the required test; unsupported text remains blocked.
The verifier self-test covers the exact accepted command, its command and argument mapping, and representative rejected near-miss and mutation-capable forms.
Verification policy documents the one admitted audit command and the continued fail-closed behavior.
Independent QA records a successful verifier result with changed-path and secret-boundary checks, or records a durable blocked or fail result without weakening the control.
allowedCommands: npm run verify:task -- --task SUT-AIOS-GOV-012 --verifier-agent qa-verification --verifier-model gpt-5.6-sol --acceptance-confirmed
solEscalationTriggers: Any proposal admits an npm command other than the exact npm audit --omit=dev literal.
Any proposal uses shell execution, expands arguments, invokes npm install, update, or fix, changes dependencies, or changes package manifests or lockfiles.
Audit output indicates a secret, credential, payment, privacy, production, or protected-path concern.
Independent verification cannot distinguish an unsupported command from a real audit failure.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only the safe-command parser, its self-test coverage, policy wording, and this task's evidence. Restore the prior fail-closed rejection of npm audit --omit=dev; do not alter packages, lockfiles, immutable baseline files, or prior blocked evidence.
